title: Notification deep link navigates to the app landing page instead of the record
body:
Moved from objectstack-ai/objectstack#9464's sibling card objectstack-ai/objectstack#9468 by the triage seat (file-at-destination: the notification centre and its click navigation are console UI; objectstack has no notifications service package building deep-link URLs, so link construction is client-side). Source: QA wave objectstack-ai/objectstack#9296, Tier-2C run record objectstack-ai/objectstack#9467, item `i18n.notification-localized-and-clears` clause 1, subject sha `e4e5c6e3c608b1b807c83a0d5b734f213eb1a1dd`, stock showcase.

## The defect

Opening a notification from the notification centre navigates to the **app landing page**, not to the record the notification is about. The deep link is the whole point of the notification — a user who clicks one is told which record changed and then dropped somewhere else.

## What the same click gets right, and why that matters

- **Mark-as-read fires correctly** and is server-authoritative — the notification is consumed, the badge clears, and the user has now lost the pointer to the record entirely.
- **The canonical record route renders fine**, including in a `zh-CN` session. The target is reachable; the link does not point at it.

Those two controls narrow this to link construction rather than a broken route or rendering failure — and the mark-read behaviour is what turns "annoying" into "the pointer is gone".

## What a fix has to settle

Where the deep-link target is built and why it resolves to the app root rather than the record. Pin it with a test asserting the **navigated URL**, not merely that navigation occurred — a test that only checks "the click went somewhere and mark-read fired" passes today.

If investigation shows the URL (or the record reference it needs) is missing from the server's notification payload, file that half back to objectstack-ai/objectstack with `Blocked-by:` linkage rather than widening this card.
